claims.text: Selective Laser Sintering with an optimized scanning strategy and reduced thermal load will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed SLS intervention will reduce residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed SLS intervention will produce a refined microstructure.
The proposed SLS intervention will reduce porosity.
Controlled melting and solidification of the AlCrFeNiSi powder particles will occur under the proposed SLS conditions.
Controlled melting and solidification will promote densification.
Controlled melting and solidification will promote stress relief.
The proposed process will increase yield strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed process will increase ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
An applicable process window is 50–100 W laser power.
An applicable process window is 0.1–1 m/s scanning speed.
An applicable process window is 20–50 μm layer thickness.
An applicable process window is 100–200 °C powder-bed temperature.
The proposed process is expected to be effective for AlCrFeNiSi components measuring 1–10 mm.
The proposed process is expected to be effective for components of simple-to-moderate geometric complexity.
